newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: cricket-England more prepared than NZ, says Rixon.
newsitem.headline: cricket-England more prepared than NZ, says Rixon.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Jan 17 - England will go into next week's first cricket test better prepared than the home side, according to New Zealand coach Steve Rixon.

Speaking after the naming of the New Zealand 12 for the Eden Park test starting in Auckland on Friday, Rixon said the programme for the country's leading players in the first half of the season had been far from ideal in terms of getting ready for a test series.
After New Zealand returned from their early-season tour of Sharjah and Pakistan, the players went straight into the Shell Cup one-day competition.

The top players missed the two early rounds of the four-day Shell Trophy. Since their return, the only first-class match was yesterday's Selection XI loss to England in Palmerston North by an innings and 113 runs.
England have come off a tour to Zimbabwe, where they played two first-class and two test matches.
They have also got two four-dayers to prepare for the first test against New Zealand.
"It's not ideal preparation," Rixon admitted yesterday.

"We don't need to be Einsteins to work out if you play a lot of four-day cricket prior to a test series you're going to be more adequately served for going out to play long innings and building partnerships.
"They're things that often get dissolved down with the one-day game."
In a bid to give the New Zealand players an extra two days of buildup for the test, a two-day practice game has been arranged against an Auckland 11 next Monday and Tuesday.
The New Zealand batsmen will have 115 overs at the crease, with the bowlers facing the same the next day.
"We need to get a bit of the one-day shots out of our system and that hopefully gives an opportunity for the top six batters in particular scoring between 50 and 80 each.
"That's the ideal situation, being at the crease an hour, hour-and-a-half, two hours.
"If some stay the day, so be it, I'll live with that. But I'd like to think we can at least bat the 115 out."
The changing face of the New Zealand team in recent seasons was evident in the naming of the 12 for Eden Park.
The last time the teams met in a test, at Manchester in 1994, only three players from the current squad were in the New Zealand side.
Opener Bryan Young, who only won his way back into the New Zealand team as a replacement for the injured Blair Pocock on the pre-Christmas tour of Sharjah and Pakistan, has held his place.
The other two survivors are gifted middle-order batsman Stephen Fleming and No 3 batsman Adam Parore.
Of the other eight players, just one was in the last New Zealand team, which lost the second test against Pakistan late last year, big lefthander Mark Greatbatch.

Star batsman Martin Crowe has retired, captain Ken Rutherford was dumped from the team and is now in South Africa, while Shane Thomson, Matthew Hart, Dion Nash, Chris Pringle and Michael Owens have all suffered injuries or career slumps.
Pocock's last test was the previous one on that tour, at Lord's.
